title: Nodal obstruction to conditioned-diffusion representations of the weak momentum
abstract: Quantum Schrödinger bridge constructions establish the existence of a conditioned process under a positivity hypothesis on the endpoint data, and three independent ones adopt it. We show that hypothesis fails on a definite locus once the conditioned object is the two-state amplitude $φ^*ψ$ of a pre- and post-selected pair on configuration space, and that the failure is testable on recorded data. Whenever $φ^*ψ$ has a moving zero of order $k$ across which probability flows, no diffusion of constant diffusion coefficient can both carry the conditioned density and avoid the nodal curve: the current velocity it would need grows as the inverse $2k$-th power of the distance to that curve and points toward it on one side, placing the curve at finite scale distance, so it is reached and not merely approached. Identifying the weak momentum with a bridge drift fails independently: for a free particle post-selected in position the current velocity is exactly minus the drift of the bridge to the target. The positive Doob $h$-transform and the Bernstein conditioning built on it exist wherever $φ^*ψ$ is nodeless and fail on the nodal curve. There the osmotic part of the weak momentum diverges as the inverse distance to the zero and changes sign across it with a coefficient set by $k$, while the current part stays bounded; that boundedness rests on the signed factorization of the real-envelope class and hides the obstruction from any picture built on the current velocity alone. A measured fringe visibility fixes a single length, which puts a Lorentzian of order $10^{-3}$ into the current channel reconstructed in the two-slit trajectory experiment if the contrast is limited by an off-axis zero, and nothing there if by incoherence. The results are one-dimensional, covering the separable transverse field of a two-slit geometry, not general two-dimensional vortices.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the weak momentum in quantum systems, showing that standard conditioned-diffusion models fail when the system's two-state amplitude develops nodes. The failure manifests as a divergence in the osmotic component of the weak momentum, which is a key diagnostic distinguishing the quantum reality from purely current-based classical descriptions.
main_problem: The paper investigates the limitations of applying conditioned-diffusion representations, derived from quantum Schrödinger bridges, to the weak momentum, especially when the two-state amplitude exhibits nodes.
main_result: The positivity hypothesis required by these bridges fails on a definite locus (the nodal curve), causing the osmotic part of the weak momentum to diverge while the current part remains bounded.
method: The analysis uses the Madelung decomposition of the weak momentum and compares its behavior to established quantum stochastic frameworks like Doob's $h$-transform.
model_or_system: The system involves pre- and post-selected quantum states ($\psi$ and $\phi$) and analyzes the weak momentum in the context of a two-slit geometry with separable transverse fields.
key_observables: Weak momentum components (current and osmotic parts), nodal locus of $\phi^*\psi$, and fringe visibility/contrast.
important_parameters: The order of the zero ($k$) of the two-state amplitude, and the small parameter $	heta$ in related context analyses.
main_assumptions: The results are derived for one-dimensional systems covering separable transverse fields, and the analysis distinguishes between the current velocity and the Itô drift.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes focus on mathematical derivations and conceptual failures rather than figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the failure of the positivity hypothesis required by quantum Schrödinger bridges when dealing with the two-state amplitude. It then analyzes the divergence of the osmotic part at the node, contrasting this with the bounded current part, and finally relates these findings to experimental diagnostics like fringe visibility.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical constraint on how quantum weak measurements can be modeled using classical diffusion processes, highlighting where the underlying stochastic assumptions break down.
